intro: Nicaragua, the largest country in Central America, is a land of lakes and volcanoes with a turbulent political history.

chapters.title: Early peoples
text: The Nicarao people gave the country its name. Footprints at Acahualinca, in Managua, were left about 6,000 years ago.

chapters.title: Colonial cities
text: Spain founded Granada and León in 1524; they became rival cities. Nicaragua became independent in 1821. In the 1850s an American adventurer, William Walker, made himself president until he was driven out.

chapters.title: Revolution and after
text: The Somoza family ruled from 1937 until the Sandinista revolution of 1979. In the 1980s the US-backed Contras fought the Sandinistas. Daniel Ortega returned to power in 2007; since 2018 protests have been crushed and many critics jailed or exiled. Ortega and his wife Rosario Murillo now rule as co-presidents.
